setup.app: AGI Desktop (Electron public Desktop) on macOS, pointed at the local web server at http://localhost:3000, with local Clerk test accounts
setup.what_it_is: The public AGI Desktop is an Electron shell. Its window loads the hosted web app (production https://agiworkforce.com by default). For local testing, an unpackaged build can be pointed at localhost with the AGI_CLOUD_APP_ORIGIN environment variable. AGI Code (coding sessions on local folders) runs in a bundled CLI process that the Electron shell starts.
prerequisites: macOS with pnpm available and the repository checked out at ~/Desktop/agiworkforce (docs/agent-context/commands.json:5 runs pnpm install). The docs in the files do not state a required Node or pnpm version for this path (apps/desktop/README.md:163 says Node 24 is needed only for the GPUI build).
Dependencies installed (pnpm install). The Electron dependency is electron ^44.10.2 (apps/desktop/package.json:168).

apps/web/.env.local present, with Clerk development keys and Stripe test-mode keys. The dev-accounts commands refuse to run without them (docs/development/local-test-accounts.md:70-78). The example file is apps/web/.env.local.example.
CLERK_AUTHORIZED_PARTIES set (docs/development/troubleshooting.md:62-64; apps/web/lib/validate-env.ts:68).
A running local web server (step 4 below). The Electron window loads whatever origin it is given, so the web server must be up first.
A local database for the local stack. The documents refer to it (local-test-accounts.md:41-45, 'the local database') but do not say how to start it.

steps.what: From the repository root, install workspace dependencies. The docs list this as the install command. It is not named as a heavy job in the docs.
Check that apps/web/.env.local exists and holds the Clerk development and Stripe test-mode keys. The dev-accounts commands read this file, and the local web server reads the same file.
From the repository root, create the local test accounts. This makes every account that does not exist yet. Existing accounts are left as they are.

Start the local web server in its own terminal and leave it running. Wrap it in the heavy-job lock, because dev servers are heavy jobs and only one may run at a time. The web app then serves http://localhost:3000.

steps.what: Find the account address to sign in with. The list command prints each account, its seed, its live state, and how to sign in as it.
Sign in inside the Electron window with the account address and the fixed code.
After a test session, put the account back to its seed. Conversations, projects and files survive a reset; plan, usage, credits and settings go back to the seed.

setup.sign_in: Use a seeded local test account, one per plan and one per lane (docs/development/local-test-accounts.md:30-38). Names include free, basic, premium, max, ultra, team, team-member, and lane-desktop (the top individual plan for the Desktop lane). Get the exact address from pnpm dev:accounts list (local-test-accounts.md:18). Address format: agi-dev-<name>+clerk_test@example.com. Code: 424242. The Clerk development instance accepts that fixed code for +clerk_test addresses and sends no mail (local-test-accounts.md:61-64). The Playwright helper signInAsDevAccount in apps/web/e2e/qa-capability-harness.ts is for specs, not hand testing (local-test-accounts.md:56-58). Use one account per tester or lane and reset it afterwards (local-test-accounts.md:56-58).

modes.how: Launch Electron with AGI_CLOUD_APP_ORIGIN=http://localhost:3000 (step 6 or 7) and sign in as a paid seeded account, such as premium, or lane-desktop for the Desktop lane (local-test-accounts.md:30-38). Desktop chat is Managed Cloud only: it does not accept provider API keys or expose Local/BYOK chat (docs/architecture/desktop.md:100-109). Cloud conversations and account state are shared with the web app (desktop.md:100-109). The plan a seeded account has is set by its seed, and pnpm dev:accounts reset <name> puts it back (local-test-accounts.md:17).

modes.mode: AGI Code on a local model
modes.how: In the Electron window, add a local folder to AGI Code first. A session cannot open until its folder is added (apps/desktop/electron/main.ts:797-798). A coding session runs the bundled CLI, which can use a local model set up in the CLI (docs/architecture/desktop.md:110-119 under Host Developer). The public Electron dispatcher refuses local-inference commands and reports localModels: false (docs/architecture/desktop.md:100-109; docs/architecture/desktop-local-runtime.md:14-17). The docs do not give the steps to choose or set up a local model inside the app. The Electron package lists @agiworkforce/providers-ollama and @agiworkforce/providers-lmstudio as dependencies (apps/desktop/package.json:73-74); that is the only mention of these providers.

modes.mode: AGI Code on the user's own key
modes.how: Same path as local-model Code: add a folder, then a coding session runs the bundled CLI, which can use a provider key set up in the CLI (docs/architecture/desktop.md:110-119). Desktop Cloud chat accepts no provider keys (desktop.md:100-109). Provider or tool secrets stay in the operating-system credential store (desktop.md:110-119). The baseline test protocol D-9 describes supplying a test provider key in a native secret field, with a visible provider label on turns (docs/development baseline at ~/.cache/agi-audit/leader-docs/2026-11-22/results/baseline/scripts/desktop.md:15). That is a test protocol, not a setup guide, and the docs do not describe that field in the Electron app.
modes.source: docs/architecture/desktop.md:100-119; apps/desktop/README.md:135-136 (no provider key or Local session is moved into Cloud); ~/.cache/agi-audit/leader-docs/2026-11-22/results/baseline/scripts/desktop.md:15

setup.how_to_tell_it_is_running: The web server is up when http://localhost:3000 opens the AGI web app in a browser. The docs do not give the exact ready message that next dev prints. The Electron window loads the origin it was given. With the variable set, it shows the web app at localhost:3000, not agiworkforce.com (apps/desktop/README.md:28-30; docs/architecture/desktop.md:141). The sign-in page at /login should load and accept the fixed code 424242 for a +clerk_test address (local-test-accounts.md:61-64). If the sign-in page hands off to the browser instead of loading in the window, VITE_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY is missing from the shell (desktop-local-runtime.md:346-348). If the window shows production, AGI_CLOUD_APP_ORIGIN was not set in the environment of that launch (config.ts:58-73). The docs do not describe any other visible indicator, such as the origin shown in the UI or a tray icon.
cannot_be_done_on_this_computer: A signed, notarized public release (DMG or ZIP) needs the Developer ID Application certificate (AGI AUTOMATION LLC, D2PR62RLT4) in the login keychain and an App Store Connect .p8 key file, plus notarization (docs/runbooks/desktop-electron-macos-release.md:13-17, 21-32). The local release script runs only on an Apple silicon Mac (scripts/release/build-desktop-mac-local.sh:20-25). It refuses a dirty tree, a missing certificate or an unreadable key (runbook:41-42). It never publishes (runbook:43-46), and publishing is a separate owner-approved step (runbook:45-46).

GitHub Actions release (.github/workflows/release-desktop-cloud.yml) needs the macos-release environment secrets APPLE_CERTIFICATE, APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD, APPLE_API_KEY, APPLE_API_ISSUER and APPLE_API_PRIVATE_KEY (runbook:50-55). Environment secrets on a private repository need a paid GitHub plan (runbook:54-55). Not on this machine.

Post-release verification on a Mac that did not build the release: codesign --verify, spctl --assess and xcrun stapler validate, install from the published DMG, and an update check (runbook:57-62). The runbook requires a different Mac for this step.

Auto-update to a newer signed build needs an already-published newer signed build (docs/development/desktop baseline D-10: ~/.cache/agi-audit/leader-docs/2026-11-22/results/baseline/scripts/desktop.md:15-16). The baseline says to record blocked and defer to the owner if none exists.

Its Cloud mode signs in through Clerk and calls the web backend; with the local env file it points at http://localhost:3000. The repo documents local test accounts (one per plan, made by pnpm dev:accounts) for trying Cloud on the Free plan or a subscribed plan without touching production.
prerequisites: Repository at ~/Desktop/agiworkforce with dependencies installed by `pnpm install` (docs/agent-context/commands.json, repoWide.install).
pnpm available (all documented commands are pnpm scripts: package.json, docs/agent-context/commands.json).

apps/mobile/.env.local present with APP_ENV=development, EXPO_PUBLIC_APP_ENV=development, EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://localhost:3000 (apps/mobile/.env.local:1-3; template at apps/mobile/.env.local.example:1-9).
apps/web/.env.local present: the dev-accounts commands read it, and the local web server reads it (docs/development/local-test-accounts.md:20-22).
The local web server running on localhost:3000 (docs/development/local-test-accounts.md:61; apps/mobile/.env.local.example:9). The docs do not state a port setting for next dev.

For the iOS Simulator: Xcode. The store runbook says the local simulator builds were made with Xcode 27.1 (docs/runbooks/mobile-store-first-release.md:85). The docs do not give an install or minimum version.

Every heavy job (dev server, Metro, simulator, emulator, build) goes through scripts/dev/heavy-job.sh, one at a time, because the machine has 16 GB (CLAUDE.md, Delegation section; scripts/dev/heavy-job.sh lines 2-4).

steps.what: Start the local web server. Each command is wrapped in the heavy-job lock as the repo requires. The web dev script runs next dev.
Make the local test accounts on the local stack. Run from the repo root. This is idempotent: existing accounts are left as they are. It is not in the heavy-job list, so it runs unwrapped.
List the accounts, their plans and how to sign in as each one. The list output is the source of truth for names.

Check the local mobile env file. It must set the API URL to localhost:3000 and the APP_ENV values. The template says to copy .env.local.example to .env.local; the working copy already exists in the tree. The file is not a command.
Start the Expo dev server (Metro) for the mobile app, wrapped in the heavy-job lock.
Build and launch the app on the iOS Simulator. This is a local native build through expo run:ios; it is heavy and must be wrapped.
Build and launch the app on the Android emulator. The docs name only the command; the emulator setup is not documented.

Optional, for a physical iPhone only. The script refuses to run without an Apple Development signing identity for the AGI team. It also runs an expo prebuild with --clean, which regenerates the native ios folder.

steps.what: Sign in as a local test account (see sign_in below). Then check the mode and plan in the app. The docs do not give the exact control labels.
Reset one account to its seed between runs, so plan, usage, credits and settings go back. Conversations, projects and files survive a reset.
For the age step, clear the five adult_eligibility_* columns on the account's profiles row in the local database and sign in again. Re-run the reset command to restore the decision.

setup.sign_in: Local test accounts are Clerk development-instance users with the address agi-dev-<name>+clerk_test@example.com. Open http://localhost:3000/login in a browser, enter that address and the code 424242. The Clerk development instance accepts that fixed code for +clerk_test addresses and sends no mail (docs/development/local-test-accounts.md:61-64). The name comes from pnpm dev:accounts list (md:18). Accounts: free, basic, premium, max, ultra, team, team-member, extra-usage, window-nearly-full, stripe-premium, lane-chrome, lane-vscode, lane-desktop, lane-cli, lane-mobile, lane-credits (md:30-39). The mobile app's own sign-in is described only as an "actual browser handoff" in the baseline (scripts/mobile.md, M-1). The 424242 code is documented for the web /login page only.

modes.how: The app needs no account. Start the mobile app with the steps above and choose the Local mode in the app. Local mode is also documented as needing no account and running the model on the device (docs/runbooks/mobile-store-first-release.md:59). The baseline's M-7 needs a compatible local model downloaded while online, then the device set offline; the files do not say how the model is downloaded or where the Local control is. A simulator can check the UI only, not the real on-device model result (scripts/mobile.md M-7, line 13).

Start the app as above. Sign in with the free account (agi-dev-free+clerk_test@example.com, code 424242 at localhost:3000/login). setup.app: AGI Chrome extension (manifest name "AGI Extension", package @agiworkforce/extension), tested against the local web server at http://localhost:3000
setup.what_it_is: The AGI Chrome extension is a Manifest V3 side panel that chats with AGI Managed Cloud and, on sites the user approves, reads and acts on the page. For local testing, Vite builds it into apps/extension/dist, Google Chrome loads that folder unpacked, and the extension and the web app both point at http://localhost:3000.
prerequisites: Node 24 and the pnpm pinned by packageManager (CONTRIBUTING.md:10-13; apps/extension/package.json:74-77 requires node >=24.0.0 and pnpm >=9.15.3).
Google Chrome 132 or later (docs/runbooks/chrome-web-store-publish.md:296; apps/extension/manifest.json:87). Incognito is not allowed (manifest.json:9).
Dependencies installed with pnpm install (CONTRIBUTING.md:16).

apps/web/.env.local from apps/web/.env.local.example, with Clerk development keys (NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY, CLERK_SECRET_KEY), a local DATABASE_URL and the secrets (apps/web/.env.local.example:10-24).
A local database: a Postgres URL must name 127.0.0.1, localhost, ::1, a *.localhost or a *.test host (docs/development/local-test-accounts.md:71-74).
A Stripe test-mode key; the account commands stop when it is missing or live-mode (local-test-accounts.md:76-77).
apps/extension/.env.local from apps/extension/.env.local.example (apps/extension/.env.example:4).
python3 on the PATH for scripts/dev/heavy-job.sh (scripts/dev/heavy-job.sh:4-5).

steps.what: Install the repository dependencies from the repository root.
Create apps/web/.env.local from the example. Set NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL to http://localhost:3000, fill the Clerk development keys and the local database URL. Leave CLERK_AUTHORIZED_PARTIES for step 8.

Create apps/extension/.env.local from the example. It already points the extension at localhost:3000 and needs the Clerk values for the development instance paired with the local web app. Leave CHROME_EXTENSION_PUBLIC_KEY unset.
Seed the local test accounts from the repository root. Accounts that exist are left unchanged.
List the accounts and their sign-in addresses.
Start the local web server on localhost:3000 in its own terminal. It is a dev server, so run it through the heavy-job wrapper.
steps.source: docs/agent-context/commands.json:126 (web.dev); apps/web/package.json:6 (dev = next dev); scripts/dev/heavy-job.sh:2-3; CLAUDE.md:28

steps.what: Build the extension. The build runs a main pass and a content-script pass and writes the unpacked folder to apps/extension/dist. Wait for it to finish.

In Chrome, open chrome://extensions, turn on Developer mode (top right), choose Load unpacked, and select apps/extension/dist. The runbook says to pick the candidate folder; dist as the local folder is inferred from vite.config.ts:63.

Copy the extension ID from its card in chrome://extensions. Add chrome-extension://<extension-id> to CLERK_AUTHORIZED_PARTIES in apps/web/.env.local, next to http://localhost:3000. Then restart the web server (the restart is not stated in the docs).
Pin the extension from the puzzle-piece menu. Open the side panel from the toolbar icon or with Command+Shift+K.
After any change to the extension source or apps/extension/.env.local, run the build again and reload the unpacked extension.
Optional, for artifact previews only: run the isolated artifact renderer on port 3002 with the unpacked extension ID. It is a second local server, so run it through heavy-job too.

setup.sign_in: The web app's local sign-in is documented: open http://localhost:3000/login, enter the account address agi-dev-<name>+clerk_test@example.com (name from pnpm dev:accounts list) and the code 424242. Clerk's development instance accepts that code for +clerk_test addresses and sends no mail (docs/development/local-test-accounts.md:61-64). Accounts are: free, basic, premium, max, ultra, team, team-member, extra-usage, window-nearly-full, stripe-premium, lane-chrome, lane-vscode, lane-desktop, lane-cli, lane-mobile, lane-credits (local-test-accounts.md:30-39). Reset an account with pnpm dev:accounts reset <name> rather than sharing one (local-test-accounts.md:17, :58-59). The side panel is signed in through the web session, because the extension reads the sync host's session cookie (apps/extension/docs/threat-model.md:57; apps/extension/.env.local.example:13 sets CLERK_SYNC_HOST=http://localhost:3000). The order "web login first, then open the side panel" is inferred from those two, not stated in the docs. The docs give no side-panel sign-in steps for local dev; the only in-panel steps are the production candidate checks (chrome-web-store-publish.md:303-304).

modes.mode: Cloud (Managed Cloud chat, following the signed-in web account)
modes.how: No Cloud switch or label is documented. Chrome chat is Managed-Cloud-only with no Local, BYOK or native fallback, so there is nothing to choose. To send extension chat to the local web server, set VITE_AGI_WEB_API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:3000 in apps/extension/.env.local (the example already does), rebuild, and reload. The chat gateway is FREE_TRIAL_GATEWAY = configuredAgiWebOrigin() ?? DEFAULT_AGI_WEB_ORIGIN, and a localhost http origin is accepted.

modes.mode: Permission modes (Auto default, Ask first, YOLO) for actions, not the Cloud chat runtime
modes.how: Auto is the default and stops for crucial actions. Ask first confirms every action; choose it in the permission menu to test approval cards. Start a task with -yolo or --always-approve for unattended YOLO on approved sites.

The toolbar icon has the title AGI Extension (manifest.json:59). The side panel shows the sign-in prompt, then the account and plan after sign-in. If sign-in appears to succeed but API calls return 401 and the panel falls back to sign-in, the CLERK_AUTHORIZED_PARTIES origin is missing (chrome-web-store-publish.md:175-177).
